title: Tejimola
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Tejimola
cast.description: Young girl, gentle; sings sadly as a spirit

cast.name: Stepmother
cast.description: Jealous, cruel stepmother, cold and sharp

cast.name: The merchant
cast.description: Tejimola's father, a loving merchant, grieving then joyful

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Assamese tradition. It is from Burhi Aair Xadhu, Grandmother's Tales, collected by Lakshminath Bezbaroa in 1911. It is called... Tejimola.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tejimola was the only daughter of a merchant in a village on the Brahmaputra. Her mother had died, and her father had married again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When he left for a long trading voyage, he asked his new wife to care for the girl as her own.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [darker] But the stepmother resented Tejimola's sweetness, and the way the neighbours loved her. When a friend invited Tejimola to a wedding, the stepmother handed her a bundle of fine clothes.

lines.speaker: stepmother
lines.text: [sweetly false] Wear these, child. Look beautiful.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [ominous] She had hidden a mouse and a burning coal inside. At the wedding, the clothes were found chewed and scorched.

lines.speaker: stepmother
lines.text: [cold fury] Careless girl! Do you know what those cost?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [softly, grave] In her rage, she crushed the girl in the dheki, the wooden rice-pounder. Then she buried her in the garden.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A gourd vine sprang up from the spot. When a beggar woman tried to pick a gourd, a voice sang from it.

lines.speaker: tejimola
lines.text: [singing softly, sad] Do not pick me, I am Tejimola... my stepmother pounded me in the dheki.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stepmother tore the vine out and threw it away. Where it fell grew a plum tree, and the cowherd boys who reached for its fruit heard the same song.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She cut down the tree. And from the river where she threw it... bloomed a lotus.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [hopeful] At last, the merchant's boat came home along the river. Seeing the beautiful lotus, he reached for it, and the flower sang to him.

lines.speaker: tejimola
lines.text: [singing softly] Do not pick me, Father... I am Tejimola.

lines.speaker: merchant
lines.text: [trembling] Tejimola? If you are truly my Tejimola... come to me as a bird.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small bird flew onto his palm.

lines.speaker: merchant
lines.text: [tearful] Then come back to me... as my daughter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [joyful] And she became his daughter again. The stepmother, seeing the girl return, fled the village in shame, and Tejimola grew up in her father's house.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [gently] Tejimola is a story about innocence that cannot be buried. Nature itself keeps singing the truth. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
